This intra-Court appeal by 286 appellants is directed against judgment dated 09.10.2023 passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court ['the Writ Court'] in WP(C) No. 924/2023 titled Abdul Hameed Bhat And Others vs Ut Of Jammu And Kashmir Through Chief ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173180919/
1 'Abdul Hamid Bhat and others vs UT of Jammu and Kashmir and others' whereby the Writ Court has declared the appellants as 'Kamas' entitled to payment of compensation/improvement charges,
to be reassessed by the respondents on the basis of parameters, to be taken into account as per rules.

sentences.text:
The plea of the appellants, that they are tenants qua land measuring 1500 kanals and 19 marlas covered by different survey numbers in estate Rakhe Gund Aksha and entitled to compensation to be assessed under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ['2013 Act'], has been rejected.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ['2013 Act']
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Writ Court has also refused to quash Government Order No.298-HUD dated 12.10.2018, a communication of the Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir dated 06.03.2022 and an advertisement notice dated 15.02.2023 issued by the Srinagar Development Authority which were subject matter of challenge in the writ petition.

2. Before we advert to the grounds of challenge urged by Mr. G.A.Lone, learned counsel appearing for the appellants to assail the judgment of the Writ Court, we deem it appropriate to state few material facts which are germane to the disposal of controversy raised in this appeal.

3. With the mechanisation of Armed Forces, the land (Farms and Rakhs) controlled by the Military Farms Department was transferred to the Revenue Department of the then State of Jammu and Kashmir vide J&K Army Command Order No. 376 dated 04.04.1949.

The Revenue Department,
after taking over the land from the Army, handed over the management and control thereof, to the Rakhs and Farms Department of the Government of Jammu and Kashmir.

It is contended by the appellants that during the year 1949, the then State of Jammu and Kashmir was facing acute shortage of food stuffs and to meet such shortage, it promulgated 'Grow More Food Scheme' to be implemented by providing different parcels out of the said land that had become available from Military Farms Department to the marginal/ small farmers, landless and needy persons in the nearby localities.
It is the case of the appellants that the said land came to be handed over to the appellants for cultivation as tenants.

It is claimed that the land allotted to the predecessors-in-interest of the appellants was marshy and waterlogged and it was with great efforts and hard work put in by the predecessors-in- interest of the appellants, the same was made cultivable.

The appellants, as is claimed by them in their petition, were entitled to ownership rights qua the land allotted to them under Government Order No. LB-6/c PF 1958 dated 05.06.1958 read with Government Order No. S-432 of 1966 dated 03.06.1966, but that did not happen due to apathy of the Government.
In the year 2000, the Government transferred the entire chunk of 4200 kanals of land to Srinagar Development Authority on payment of development charges.

The appellants claim that notwithstanding the written transfer of land from Rakhs and Farms Department to Srinagar Development Authority, the land continued to remain under their cultivation as tenants paying 1/4th share of the produce or its value to the Government.

4. Feeling aggrieved by the unilateral transfer of the land under occupation of the appellants to Srinagar Development Authority, the appellants filed a civil suit titled 'Mehdi Mir and others vs.
State and others'.

sentences.text: Apart from challenging the transfer of land, the appellants also claimed other reliefs to protect their possession.
The appellants also filed a suit for permanent prohibitory injunction titled 'Mehdi Mir and others vs. State and others' in the Court of Sub- Judge Srinagar.

They fairly submit that both the suits were not pursued and were later on dismissed for Abdul Hameed Bhat And Others vs Ut Of Jammu And Kashmir Through Chief ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173180919/
2 non-prosecution.

sentences.text: However, the applications for restoration of both the suits are pending adjudication before the civil Court(s).

As it seems, the appellants, after abandoning the suits, filed the instant petition being triggered to do so by a Notification dated 15.2.2023 issued by the Srinagar Development Authority inviting applications from the general public for registration of residential plots intended for construction of residential houses over part of land in possession of the appellants.

The advertisement notification, as is apparent from its perusal, shows that a Satellite Township is proposed to be constructed in Rakhe Gund Aksha which is the land under possession of the appellants.
5. The writ petition was contested by respondent No.4 and 5.

In the reply affidavit filed by the then Vice-Chairman, Srinagar Development Authority, it is submitted that vide Government Order No.
191 HUD of 2000 dated 24.08.2000, land measuring 4200 kanals and 19 marlas falling in different khasra numbers of village Rakh Gund Akasha, Tehsil and District Srinagar ['the subject land'] was transferred to Srinagar Development Authority for development of a Housing Colony under phase II.

Out of the land transferred to Srinagar Development Authority, the Government vide Government Order No. 222 HUD of 2019 dated 25.10.2019 and Government order No. 156 HUD of 2020 dated 6.6.2020 transferred land measuring 500 kanals in favour of Department of Law,
Justice and Parliamentary Affairs for construction of Jammu and Kashmir High Court Complex at Rakhe Gund Aksha.

entities.text: Jammu and Kashmir High Court Complex
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Similarly, vide another Government order dated 17.03.2022, land measuring 750 kanals out of the aforesaid land was transferred by the Government to the Industries Department for setting up Medicity.

It is further submitted by respondents 4 and 5 in the reply affidavit that the writ petition was not maintainable as the appellants had suppressed the material facts from the Court and had not disclosed clearly that on the subject matter, they had already filed two civil suits having been dismissed for non-prosecution by the concerned civil Courts.

It is submitted by the Srinagar Development Authority that initially the Revenue Department, in pursuance of Cabinet decision No. 140/12 dated 18.08.2000, issued Government order No. 132- HUD of 2001 dated 28.05.2001 providing for payment of improvement charges by the Srinagar Development Authority to the occupants/Kamas at the rate of Rs.40,000/- per kanal for the subject land.

However, vide Government order dated 12.10.2018, the Government accorded sanction to the payment of enhanced improvement charges to the Kamas of left over land of 3760 kanals transferred to Srinagar Development Authority for setting up a Satellite township at Rakhe Gund Aksha at the rate of Rs.60,000/- per kanal for non-irrigated non- paddy fields and Rs.1.20 lac per kanal for abi awal paddy land.

It is, thus, submitted that in the absence of any challenge to these orders, the appellants are not entitled to claim the improvement charges to the tune of Rs.12.00 lacs per kanal as a matter of right.

It is an emphatic stand taken by Srinagar Development Authority that the land transferred to it was Government land and, therefore, the Government was not supposed to acquire its own land and pay compensation to the persons in its unauthorised occupation.

A clear stand, however, taken in the reply affidavit is that the petitioners-appellants herein are only Kamas qua the land and not the owners, therefore, cannot dictate their terms to claim the improvement charges at the rate of Rs.12.00 lacs per kanal.
There is, however, no reply affidavit filed by other respondents.

6 In the light of rival contentions and the material placed on record by both the sides,
the Writ Court considered the matter at some length and concluded that the appellants had failed to demonstrate that they were the tenants qua the subject land and, therefore, entitled to compensation, to be assessed under 2013 Act.

The Writ Court, however, accepted the stand of Abdul Hameed Bhat And Others vs Ut Of Jammu And Kashmir Through Chief ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173180919/
3 Srinagar Development Authority that appellants were the occupants/Kamas of the subject land and therefore, entitled to improvement charges.

entities.text: Abdul Hameed Bhat And Others vs Ut Of Jammu And Kashmir Through Chief
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Writ Court, however, opined that the improvement charges were worked out way back in the year 2001 and, therefore, there was need to reassess the improvement charges to be paid to the appellants and, accordingly, issued directions for reassessment and payment of improvement charges to the appellants within a period of two months.
It is this judgment of the Writ Court the appellants are aggrieved of and have filed the instant appeal.
7 Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.

8 As is indicative from para (22) of the impugned judgment, the Writ Court was called upon to adjudicate following two issues:
(i). Whether the appellants are tenants as is claimed by them or Kamas of the subject land as is the stand of the respondents.
(ii) If the appellants are held not to be tenants, but as Kamas, were they be entitled to Rs.12.00 lacs of compensation/improvement charges per kanal as claimed by the appellants.

9 From the material on record, in particular the documents placed on record by the appellants along with their petition, there is no clarity as to status of the appellants vis-a-vis the subject matter.

After the land was transferred by the Department of Military Farms of Indian Army to the Revenue Department of the then State of Jammu and Kashmir, the land came under the control of Farms and Rakh Department of the State.
It was a big chunk of land measuring more than 5200 kanals of land situate in estate Rakhe Gund Aksha.
The appellants have not been in a position to demonstrate as to how they came in possession of aforesaid land which, of course, is in their possession for more than 6/7 decades.

The appellants claim that they were inducted in the subject land as tenants by the Government on payment of rent to the extent of 1/4th of the produce of crops or value thereof to the Government through Rakhs and Farms Department.
The respondents deny this aspect and submit that they had of their own occupied the subject land and were treated as Kamas qua subject land.

The plea of the appellants is that being tenants of the subject land, they have interest in the land and, therefore, cannot be evicted by the Government without payment of compensation, to be assessed in terms of 2013 Act.

On the other hand, the plea of the respondents is that the appellants are not the tenants, but Kamas and, therefore, are entitled only to the payment of improvement charges as determined by the Government vide Government Order dated 20.05.2001 revised vide Government order dated 12.10.2018.

So far as the challenge of the appellants to the transfer of land under their occupation to SDA is concerned, learned counsel appearing for the appellants made a statement before the Writ Court that the appellants (petitioners in the writ petition) were not opposing the transfer of land or development of a Satellite township.

10 So far as the question of status of the appellants/writ petitioners qua the subject land is concerned, the Writ Court has dismissed the petition on the ground that the same is not maintainable in view of the issue having been specifically raised in the two suits before the civil Courts which, later on, came to be dismissed for non prosecution.

The Writ Court, after referring to the provisions of Order 9 Rule 9 of CPC and some judgments of the Supreme Court, concluded that Abdul Hameed Bhat And Others vs Ut Of Jammu And Kashmir Through Chief ...

the writ petition, on the same cause of action on which two civil suits stood filed by the appellants before the civil Courts which were later on dismissed for non prosecution, was barred and not maintainable.
It is this issue determined by the Writ Court which is vehemently agitated by learned counsel for the appellants.
11 With a view to appreciating the arguments of Mr. Lone, it would be appropriate to refer to two civil suits filed by the appellants before the civil Courts.

12 From a reading of plaints placed on record by the appellants through the medium of CM No.
7559/2023 filed in this appeal, it transpires that feeling aggrieved by the Government order dated 24.08.2000 (supra) whereby the subject land under occupation of the appellants was transferred to Srinagar Development Authority on payment of improvement charges as fixed by the Revenue Department, 147 persons out of the appellants filed a suit for declaration to the effect that the Government order dated 24.08.2000 was against the tenancy rights of the appellants and, therefore,
deserved to be declared against the spirit of law.
The aforesaid appellants also prayed for a decree of declaration that they be declared as owners of the property and not liable to be evicted from the land under their occupation forcibly.

In the aforesaid suit filed before the Court of Principal District Judge, Srinagar, the appellants essentially sought a declaration to the effect that they were the protected tenants qua the subject land and, therefore, could not be thrown out or evicted being protected by the tenancy laws.

entities.text: Court of Principal District Judge, Srinagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: They also sought a decree of declaration to the effect that Government Order dated 24.08.2000 (supra) was against the spirit of law.

The cause of action to file the aforesaid suit, though not specifically pleaded, accrued to the appellants when in the year 2000, the Government transferred the subject land to SDA for development of a Satellite township on payment of improvement charges as determined by the Revenue Department and the appellants were sought to be evicted.

In the second suit by same 147 appellants, they have prayed for permanent injunction restraining the defendants not to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit land as protected tenants in the garb of Government order dated 24.08.2000.
The second suit is also on the same cause of action.
As is claimed, the cause of action accrued to the appellants when SDA started interfering in their peaceful possession.

Be that as it may, both the suits have been filed by the appellants on the cause of action that accrued to them upon issuance of Government order dated 24.08.2000 transferring the land under their occupation to SDA on payment of improvement charges as may be determined by the Revenue Department and proposed eviction of the appellants for establishing a Satellite Colony.

The writ petition filed is substantially on the same cause of action, the only addition being that the SDA has also issued an advertisement notice inviting applications from the eligible persons for registration of plots in the proposed colony.

The Writ Court has, thus, rightly concluded that the writ petition filed by the appellants is primarily and essentially based on the same cause of action on which two suits were filed by the appellants before the civil Courts which were dismissed for non prosecution.

13 We are neither adverting to the provisions of Order 9 Rule 8 and 9 of CPC, nor shall be referring to the case law on the point, for, the Writ Court has not only reproduced the aforesaid provisions and discussed the case law extensively,
but has also compared the cause of action that accrued to the appellants for filing two civil suits and the cause of action that is basis of filing of the writ petition and concluded that the cause of action in both is substantially the same.

Needless to reiterate that Order 9 Rule 9 CPC clearly provides that where a suit is dismissed for non prosecution under Rule 8 of CPC, the plaintiff shall be precluded from bringing a fresh suit in respect of same cause of action.

The same cause of action as is explained by the Supreme Court in the context of provisions of Order 9 Rule 9 CPC, would mean Abdul Hameed Bhat And Others vs Ut Of Jammu And Kashmir Through Chief ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173180919/
5 that the cause of action in the suit dismissed for non prosecution and the cause of action in the subsequent suit or proceedings is same in substance and may not be technically identical.

entities.text: Abdul Hameed Bhat And Others vs Ut Of Jammu And Kashmir Through Chief
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14 We concur with the conclusions drawn by the Writ Court and hold that the writ petition at the instance of at least 147 appellants was barred by the principle enshrined in Order 9 Rule 9 of CPC.

15 Mr. Lone learned counsel for the appellants has, however, raised an interesting point and submits that the writ petitioners before the Writ Court were 286 and only 147 were the plaintiffs in the two suits dismissed for non prosecution and, therefore, the appellants (writ petitioners) other than 147 plaintiffs in the suit cannot be debarred from raising their grievance by way of a writ petition.
16 We have given our thoughtful consideration to this aspect of the matter and we find that in respect of persons similarly situated, there could not be two contradictory orders or judgments.

The applications for restoration of the suits are pending before the Court below and in case the restoration applications are allowed and the suits are restored to its original number, the plaintiffs therein shall be well within their right to pursue their claim and establish that they are the tenants and, therefore, entitled to be compensated for deprivation of their tenancy rights by the Government/SDA and nothing said in the judgment impugned would prejudice their such rights.
So far as the appellants other 147 plaintiffs in the suits are concerned, they have missed the bus by having failed to challenge the Government Order of 2000 (supra) within reasonable time.
The writ petition challenging the Government order of 2000 (supra) which is the basis of cause of action to the appellants is otherwise barred by delay and laches.

We are, however, in agreement with the Writ Court that the improvement charges, which were assessed by the Revenue Department in the year 2001 and revised in the year 2018 are required to be re-worked and reassessed.
We are in the year 2024 and improvement charges which were worked out in the year 2018 would not be fair and reasonable.
We, therefore, are not inclined to interfere with the directions issued by the Writ Court to reassess the improvement charges payable to the writ petitioners.

We, however, hasten to add that while computing the improvement charges, the Revenue Department shall keep in mind that the appellants had been in permissive possession of the subject land for the last more than 6-7 decades and the subject land had been a source of their livelihood.

The Revenue Department, while determining the improvement charges as per rules and norms, shall also pay a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
per kanal as a cost of rehabilitation.
This will render justice to the appellants.

We would like to make it clear that if 147 appellants who were the plaintiffs in the civil suits also intend to take the benefit of this judgment, they shall be free to withdraw their applications for restoration and apply to the Revenue Department to determine their compensation as per this judgment.

17 For the foregoing reasons, we dispose of this appeal by (i) that the appeal in respect of 147 appellants, who were plaintiffs before the civil Courts in two suits, is not maintainable and the same is, accordingly, dismissed
. The judgment of the Writ Court to that extent is upheld.
They shall, however, be at liberty to pursue the restoration applications which are stated to have been filed by them and are pending consideration of the civil Courts concerned;
(ii) that the appeal with regard to rest of the appellants is also held not maintainable being barred by delay and laches.
